subject: transport.set_tempo on a project holding more than one tempo event
question: set_tempo verifies by reading the tempo field it just typed into. Is a field holding the typed value the same fact as Logic having applied it?

reverify.command: Manual, and it mutates: with ONE tempo event, drive `logic_transport.set_tempo` and read the Tempo list. Then place the playhead somewhere sub-bar, press `새로운 템포 이벤트 생성` so the project holds TWO, drive `set_tempo` again, and read the Tempo list AND Logic's window list. Dismiss the alert, raise the arrange window by title, and undo.
reverify.expected: With one event the call answers State A and the Tempo list moves. With two it answers State C `ax_write_failed` carrying `blocking_modal: informational_alert` and `modal_raised_by_this_write: true`, the Tempo list does NOT move, and a modal `경고` window is present. Before the fix the second case answered State A with `verified: true`.

method: Driven against a release binary talking to live Logic. The two conditions differ in ONE thing — how many tempo events the project holds — and the same call is made in both, so the reading separates the operation from the project state. The effect was read from the Tempo list, a surface independent of the field the operation writes and verifies against, and Logic's window list was read in the same pass so the alert is an observation rather than an inference. The project was returned to one event at 120 and re-read to confirm.

observations.what: what a blind review found in the FIRST version of the fix, and what replaced it
observations.first_rule: refuse when the classified modal KIND differs before and after the write
three_ways_that_was_wrong: ModalReconciliation.classify answers .none for an UNREADABLE read — every signal it takes defaults to false — so the original false State A survived every failed after-read
a kind CHANGE (strayMenu -> informationalAlert) is not evidence this write caused anything
one informational alert REPLACED by another compares equal and slips through
also_found: the geometry-free direct AX write returned State B with no modal reading at all
Escape was pressed before any modal scan, and Escape can clear the very alert that is the evidence
observations.rule_now: State A requires a COMPLETE modal read that is clean. A blocker present at all — whoever raised it — means the field cannot be read as the project's tempo, and an incomplete read means we do not know. Both refuse. The before-reading survives only as an annotation (`blocker_present_before_write`) and is not load-bearing.

mutation_checks.disable the completeness check: the unreadable-scan test goes red with State A verified:true observed 130
mutation_checks.disable the presence check: the alert test goes red with State A verified:true observed 144

conclusion: A tempo field holding the typed value is NOT the project holding that tempo. On a project with more than one tempo event, Logic refuses the control-bar tempo edit and says so with a single-button modal alert directing the caller to the Tempo List editor — and `set_tempo` answered State A with `verified: true` and `observed: 144` while both tempo rows stayed at 120. Every success branch verified against the same field it had written, which cannot tell a refusal from a success. The fix requires a COMPLETE, clean modal read before it will answer State A. A first version compared the classified kind before and after and refused on a difference; a blind review showed that inference cannot be made sound — an unreadable read classifies as `.none` and let the original false State A through, a kind change is not causation, and a replaced alert of the same kind compares equal — so the claim was narrowed to one this function can support. The alert also wedged everything that followed it — undo, the audio-import panel, and three separate delete paths — which is why several earlier readings in this session were taken against a blocked Logic.
limits: The fix makes the operation HONEST, not capable. A project with two tempo events still cannot have its tempo written through this operation; it now says so instead of claiming success. Whether the Tempo List editor offers a writable path was not measured.

One locale. The alert was identified by its shape — a top-level AXDialog with exactly one button — and never by its Korean text, so the fix is locale-independent, but that was reasoned rather than measured on a second locale.
Two tempo events, both at 120 bpm. Nothing here says what happens with three, or with events at different tempos.

The exposure SHAPE was counted, the exposure was not. 21 of the 40 State A sites under `Sources/LogicProMCP/Channels` sit in the 10 files that never read Logic's modal state, and `mixer.set_volume` declares `verify_source: "ax_slider"` — it reads the fader it wrote, exactly the shape that made this defect. But a shape is not a defect: the REFUSAL here is specific (Logic objects to a control-bar tempo edit when the project holds more than one tempo event), and no other operation was driven to find out whether Logic ever answers it with a dialog. Nothing here says those 21 sites are wrong; it says a refusal of this kind could not be detected at them.
It does not DISMISS the blocker. The refusal reports it and stops; clearing it is the preflight reconciler's job on the next operation, and whether that actually runs on this path was not driven.

The gate now refuses while ANY blocker is up, including one this call did not cause. That is a deliberate false-negative: a stuck dialog makes every tempo write report `ax_write_failed` with `blocker_present_before_write: true` until it is cleared. Refusing to verify through a blocked Logic is the honest half of the trade, and the annotation tells the caller which problem to fix.
